view: Not a problem yet in aggregate, but both years are at or near the amber line. Tracked delays and cancellations total ~1.4 GW for 2027 (~5.5% of our 26 GW US base; most of it is Starbase's power permit, which a larger permit would reverse) and ~2.8 GW for 2028 (~9% of 31 GW), plus ~2.9 GW at risk in 2028. That is close to Morgan Stanley (4.9 GW in 2028) and well inside our 2028 bear case (18 GW). The new pattern is legal: open-meetings suits (Botetourt, Dazzler, PW Gateway) can undo approvals, and developers now walk from approved sites (Vantage). Watch the January Effingham vote, Texas 2027 legislation, and whether Botetourt-style suits spread.
rules: Delayed = enjoined, court-halted, paused for 3+ months or pushed a year. Lost = cancelled, denied or withdrawn (relocated counts until a new site is named). At risk = active opposition, missing permit or financing, not yet delayed. Year = the year first power was due; assumed 2028 where not disclosed. MW basis varies (IT, peak, campus) and is noted per row.

street: ~12 GW of the US pipeline at risk through 2030 from tighter TX/OH rules: 4.9 GW (2028), 3.8 GW (2029), 3.7 GW (2030); ~4% of 2028 and ~7% of 2029 capacity; 2027 unaffected. Separately ~5 GW of 2028 shifts to 2029.
Of ~21 GW inside US moratorium areas, only ~2.3 GW actually delayed (excluding the Texas pause); ~80% of restrictions cover no modelled capacity.
2028: ~30 GW in election states exposed to pauses under pro-moratorium outcomes vs 5.7 GW otherwise (exposure, not a forecast).
~30 GW, or 34% of 2028–30 capacity, could be affected by local opposition (TX, GA, OH); opposition polling up from 42% to 75% in a year.
10–15 GW of the ~43 GW expected online in 2027 may not come online (opinion).
At least 75 US projects worth ~$130B blocked or delayed in 1Q26, the most since tracking began; opposition groups more than doubled to 833.
Share of planned US capacity in states whose governors back a pause: OpenAI ~100% (14 GW), Microsoft ~45%, Amazon ~42%, Anthropic and Google ~20s%.
